cases.sentence: – Только не я, – смутившись и бросив ___ на стоявшего подле с Сергеем Ивановичем ядовитого господина, сказал Свияжский.
cases.explain: «испуганный взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Certainly not I,” said Sviazhsky, looking confused, and turning an alarmed glance at the malignant gentleman, who was standing beside Sergey Ivanovitch.

cases.sentence: Борьба! – сказал он, нахмурившись и сжав свои ___.
cases.explain: «сильные скулы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, it is keenly exciting,” said Vronsky. “And once taking the thing up, one’s eager to see it through. It’s a fight!” he said, scowling and setting his powerful jaws.

cases.sentence: – А как это вы – постоянный ___ и не мировой судья?
cases.explain: «деревенский житель» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “How is it that you, living constantly in the country, are not a justice of the peace? You are not in the uniform of one.”

cases.sentence: – Оттого, что я считаю, что ___ есть дурацкое учреждение, – отвечал мрачно Левин, все время ждавший случая разговориться с Вронским, чтобы загладить свою грубость при первой встрече.
cases.explain: «мировой суд» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s because I consider that the justice of the peace is a silly institution,” Levin answered gloomily. He had been all the time looking for an opportunity to enter into conversation with Vronsky, so as to smooth over his rudeness at their first meeting.

cases.sentence: – Я этого не полагаю, напротив, – со ___ сказал Вронский.
cases.explain: «спокойным удивлением» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I don’t think so, quite the contrary,” Vronsky said, with quiet surprise.

cases.sentence: – Это игрушка, – перебил его Левин. – ___ нам не нужны.
cases.explain: «Мировые судьи» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s a plaything,” Levin cut him short. “We don’t want justices of the peace. I’ve never had a single thing to do with them during eight years. And what I have had was decided wrongly by them. The justice of the peace is over thirty miles from me. For some matter of two roubles I should have to send a lawyer, who costs me fifteen.”

cases.sentence: – Я не понимаю, – сказал Сергей Иванович, заметивший неловкую выходку брата, – я не понимаю, как можно быть до такой степени лишенным всякого ___.
cases.explain: «политического такта» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I can’t understand,” said Sergey Ivanovitch, who had observed his brother’s clumsiness, “I can’t understand how anyone can be so absolutely devoid of political tact. That’s where we Russians are so deficient. The marshal of the province is our opponent, and with him you’re ami cochon, and you beg him to stand. Count Vronsky, now … I’m not making a friend of him; he’s asked me to dinner, and I’m not going; but he’s one of our side—why make an enemy of him? Then you ask Nevyedovsky if he’s going to stand. That’s not a thing to do.”

cases.sentence: Подойдя к ящику, он держал шар в правой, но, подумав, что ошибся, перед ___ переложил шар в левую руку и, очевидно, потом положил налево.
cases.explain: «самым ящиком» — after the preposition «перед», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Put it in the right side,” whispered Stepan Arkadyevitch, as with his brother Levin followed the marshal of his district to the table. But Levin had forgotten by now the calculations that had been explained to him, and was afraid Stepan Arkadyevitch might be mistaken in saying “the right side.” Surely Snetkov was the enemy. As he went up, he held the ball in his right hand, but thinking he was wrong, just at the box he changed to the left hand, and undoubtedly put the ball to the left. An adept in the business, standing at the box and seeing by the mere action of the elbow where each put his ball, scowled with annoyance. It was no good for him to use his insight.

cases.sentence: Съев котлетку с фасолью и поговорив с лакеем о ___, Левин, не желая входить в залу, где ему было так неприятно, пошел пройтись на хоры.
cases.explain: «прежних господах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: As no one was paying any attention to him, and no one apparently needed him, he quietly slipped away into the little room where the refreshments were, and again had a great sense of comfort when he saw the waiters. The little old waiter pressed him to have something, and Levin agreed. After eating a cutlet with beans and talking to the waiters of their former masters, Levin, not wishing to go back to the hall, where it was all so distasteful to him, proceeded to walk through the galleries. The galleries were full of fashionably dressed ladies, leaning over the balustrade and trying not to lose a single word of what was being said below. With the ladies were sitting and standing smart lawyers, high school teachers in spectacles, and officers. Everywhere they were talking of the election, and of how worried the marshal was, and how splendid the discussions had been. In one group Levin heard his brother’s praises. One lady was telling a lawyer:

cases.sentence: Посередине залы стоял человек в мундире и тонким, ___ провозглашал:
cases.explain: «громким голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: All the noblemen were sitting railed off behind barriers according to their districts. In the middle of the room stood a man in a uniform, who shouted in a loud, high voice:
